version.changelog:
- Major documentation rewrite: SKILL.md now provides a detailed introduction, usage instructions, option flags, scoring model, risk flag definitions, output formats, CI/CD integration examples, and best practices.
- Expanded explanation of risk scoring and audit flags, including real-world code examples and clarifications on security implications.

llm.summary: The skill is internally consistent: it is a local, static linter for OpenClaw skills that only reads files under skill directories and computes hashes; it does not request unrelated credentials or perform remote actions.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (security linter) match the provided artifacts: SKILL.md documents a static auditor and the shipped bin/claw-lint.sh implements file discovery, pattern-based scanning, and optional SHA256 inventory. Required binaries listed (find, grep, sha256sum, awk, etc.) are appropriate and proportional to the task.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and the script scan ~/.openclaw/workspace/skills and ~/.openclaw/skills, read file contents for regex-based checks, and optionally compute SHA256 hashes. The tool explicitly avoids executing scanned skill code; the script itself performs only file system operations, pattern matches, and hashing. It does not reference environment variables or config paths outside the declared skill directories.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is provided (instruction-only with included script). No downloads or external installers are used; code is bundled in the skill package. This is a low-risk install model for this purpose.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires no credentials or environment secrets. It reads files under the skill directories (and $HOME for default roots) which is necessary for inventory and scanning. Declared dependencies match what the script uses; no unrelated secrets or services are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not marked always:true and does not request persistent system-wide changes or elevated privileges. It only runs as an invoked script; it does not modify other skills' configurations or the system.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent and implements a local, static linter. Before running it: (1) review bin/claw-lint.sh yourself (it will run on your machine) to confirm you accept it reading files in ~/.openclaw/* and computing hashes; (2) run it as a normal user (not root) or in a sandbox if you prefer; (3) expect regex false positives (the scanner looks for patterns like private keys, AWS vars, curl|bash, etc.); (4) JSON output requires Python 3 and the listed Unix tools; and (5) if you want to be extra cautious, verify the skill's checksum or run it against a copy of your skills directory rather than your production set.
